frase_inicial: Timothy and Melanie: you already hold 16 months of emergency cash, so let’s go step by step and use one small move.

tarjetas.frente: The high-rate card is the score blocker
tarjetas.reverso: Carrying that card costs you more than your cash earns. Clearing part of it lifts the household score and frees future income.
tarjetas.detalle: Pay $6,800 on the Chase CC (18% rate) from cash; leaves $11,200 on the card after the move.

tarjetas.frente: Life cover needs attention for Liam and Josh
tarjetas.reverso: Both incomes matter to the kids. Adding life cover reduces the gap that currently holds your published score down.
tarjetas.detalle: Add $235,000 life cover to reach $485,000 total; after card paydown life cover should reach $491,800 to meet gate.

tarjetas.frente: An umbrella policy shields your savings
tarjetas.reverso: Home and car insurance don’t cover big liability claims; umbrella cover protects the liquid saving you’ve built for the children.
tarjetas.detalle: No umbrella now; recommended $1,000,000 of umbrella cover gap.

tarjetas.frente: You have extra cash above your reserve
tarjetas.reverso: About half of your cash sits beyond the emergency cushion. That money can be used thoughtfully to reduce the most costly holes.
tarjetas.detalle: Accessible cash today: $150,800; cash above emergency reserve and near-term goals: $60,222.50.

tarjetas.frente: College for Liam and Josh is unfunded
tarjetas.reverso: No 529s yet. If you want help for college later, starting small each month keeps it realistic alongside protection moves.
tarjetas.detalle: Total college funding still needed today: $113,508.60; extra first-year saving needed: $4,609.22 per year.

tarjetas.frente: Retirement saving is on track—keep it
tarjetas.reverso: Employer matches are captured and projections hold. This strength means you can focus spare cash on protection and debt first.
tarjetas.detalle: Retirement saving steady; both employer matches fully captured ($8,000 and $6,000 yearly).

tarjetas.frente: Invested mix is hotter than Melanie prefers
tarjetas.reverso: Timothy and Melanie have different comfort with swings. Agreeing together on how much ups-and-downs to accept will make investing easier.
tarjetas.detalle: Household long-term accounts about 77% stocks versus a 60% moderate target; Timothy = Growth, Melanie = Moderate.

tarjetas.frente: Some cash could pay down expensive interest
tarjetas.reverso: Using a bit of the extra cash to cut the card reduces the interest drain and is a simple way to make money work harder for you.
tarjetas.detalle: Card interest cost at 18% versus cash earning near zero; $6,800 paydown is the plan's first move.

tarjetas.reverso: Pick the single action you both can start today so neither feels pushed: one small, joint step beats many undone ones.
